title: Jeyuk Bokkeum
subtitle: korean spicy pork stir-fry
excerpt: Jeyuk bokkeum is a Korean pork stir-fry coated in a bold gochujang and soy sauce marinade and cooked quickly over high heat until sticky and slightly charred. It is served over rice. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Jeyuk bokkeum is one of the most common pork dishes in Korean home cooking. The name means stir-fried pork in Korean. It uses a similar spiced marinade to bulgogi but with pork and more heat.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the raw marinated pork flat in a bag for up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the batch and freeze half before cooking.

glossaryTerms.definition: A Korean fermented red chilli paste made from chilli powder, glutinous rice, and fermented soybeans. It is thick, spicy, and slightly sweet.
A Korean cooking term for stir-frying. Bokkeum dishes are cooked quickly over high heat in a wok or large pan with a well-seasoned sauce.

content.text: as the main flavour base. The pork is marinated then stir-fried at high heat so the edges caramelise and char. Serves 4 over rice.
Thinly sliced pork works best. Pork loin or pork belly both work well. Ask the butcher to slice it to about 5 mm thickness, or slice it yourself from a partially frozen piece.
Mix all the marinade ingredients in a large bowl. Add the pork slices and onion. Mix well until everything is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over very high heat until smoking. Add the pork and onion mixture in a single layer. Do not stir for the first 2 minutes.
Stir-fry for a further 5 to 7 minutes, keeping the heat high, until the pork is cooked through and the edges have char marks. The sauce will reduce and cling to the meat.
Add the spring onion and toss for 1 minute. Remove from the heat.
Scatter sesame seeds over the top. Serve immediately over steamed short-grain rice with kimchi on the side.

attrs.issue: Pork is steaming rather than charring
attrs.fix: The pan is not hot enough or there is too much pork in the pan. Cook in two batches and wait until the wok is smoking before adding the meat.

attrs.issue: Sauce is burning on the wok
attrs.fix: Lower the heat slightly and add 2 tablespoons of water. The gochujang sugar content makes the sauce prone to catching on very high heat.
The pork was sliced too thick. Aim for 5 mm or thinner. Pork loin dries out quickly if overcooked, so pull it from the heat as soon as it is cooked through.

content.text: Jeyuk bokkeum is a daily meal in Korean homes and a common item in Korean lunchbox restaurants. It is one of the most popular toppings for a dolsot bibimbap. The dish is quick to make, which makes it a weeknight staple for families. It is bold enough to eat with plain rice but works equally well in wraps with lettuce and ssamjang.
